description: OpenAPI path-operation coverage, request-media alternatives, and reverse-direction exclusions.

scenarios.description: A supported path operation remains callable while every request-media declaration and webhook interaction receives its own disposition; the object-schema custom media selects no carriage lane.
A parameter/body-property collision is preserved through a binding-private transform, so both artifact-declared media alternatives remain represented.
A required body property colliding with a parameter remains independently callable and coverage-complete under the current revision.
An absolute sole server makes an ordinary path operation directly invocable without a server-selection prerequisite.
A content-form parameter outside the specification's JSON and text carriage is excluded at synthesis instead of producing an operation that can never faithfully send the declared value.
A document-level custom schema dialect excludes only operations whose projected contracts inherit it; schema-free operations and supported per-schema overrides remain faithfully synthesizable.
A generic OAS 3.0 raw-binary request body is represented for its declared concrete media type without a media-selection requirement.
OAS 3.1 schema-omitted raw bytes and schema-declared encoded text are both represented without collapsing their distinct wire carriage.
A range-only request body remains a represented protocol-blind operation while coverage records the concrete request-media choice required for invocation.
A mixed exact-plus-range request has no target-wide media requirement, while the represented range alternative records the concrete choice it needs.
An optional range-only body has no target-wide requirement because bodyless invocation is available, while its represented range alternative still requires concrete request media.
A declaration-complex exact JSON request remains fully represented through whole-value carriage rather than being excluded by the flattened router.
An exact schema-omitted OAS 3.0 raw-byte operation is fully represented without a media-selection requirement.

A multipart part declaring no `type` (a bare description) is represented UNDER THE 3.0 LINE, where no accepted edition states a default contentType row that reaches it — 3.0.0 through 3.0.3 enumerate a string with format binary, other primitive types, object, and array without a catch-all, and 3.0.4 tabulates the same cases keyed on a declared type. There openbindings.openapi@1 supplies the answer as its own convention: the part default is keyed by the supplied value's JSON application type at invocation. This scenario carried `openapi: 3.1.0` until 2026-08-17 and asserted the same representation there, which was wrong — every accepted 3.1 edition states application/octet-stream for that part, and OAPI-SS-23 and OAPI-SS-24 now pin those dispositions.

info.title: Type-absent part coverage on the 3.0 line

scenarios.description: A part schema declaring one non-null anyOf branch beside a null branch collapses to that branch's carriage and is represented, while a choice with more than one non-null branch keeps its exclusion.

file.description: The file to process; JSON null elides the part.

scenarios.description: The string-carriage lane needs both halves of a derived scope: a governing schema that resolves to type string, and a media type that is character data. A concrete non-JSON, non-form declaration meeting both is represented -- text/plain, text/csv, and XML alike -- while the same media types declared with an object schema select no lane, because no lane builds a document from an object model. A media type whose registration establishes no character encoding has no defined string-to-octets mapping, so a string-typed binary declaration keeps the byte boundary and is an excluded alternative; under OAS 3.1 format binary carries no assertion force, so that declaration resolves to a bare type string and is decided entirely by its media type. A schema that asserts nothing is the same declaration as an omitted schema and takes the artifact-authorized byte lane.

String content parses under the YAML 1.2.2 grammar pin, and its plain scalars resolve by the core schema's tag resolution: date-shaped, time-shaped and YAML 1.1 boolean-word scalars match none of the null, bool, int or float patterns, so each is a string. The restriction is the artifact authority's, which limits tags to those allowed by YAML's JSON schema ruleset, so no accepted edition carries a timestamp-tagged node. The string-carried document synthesizes exactly as its JSON spelling does.

scenarios.description: A self-recursive component is reached from the request body only through a property the OAS declares readOnly, and from the response body directly. Request projection removes the property, so the emitted input contract must not publish a definition for a component no request instance can contain, while the output contract keeps the same component as its own recursive definition. Both boundaries stay realizable and the operation is fully represented.

JSON Schema 2020-12 defines an array-valued type as a union, so a form part typed ["string", "null"] declares exactly what the collapsing anyOf spelling declares and takes the same carriage: the part is represented, its sibling keywords still apply, and a supplied JSON null elides the optional part. A part typed ["string", "object"] declares two non-null alternatives, leaves no single faithful form carriage, and is an excluded alternative -- the same answer a choice with more than one non-null branch gets. Under the OAS 3.0 line, whose Schema Object requires type to be a string and does not support multiple types via an array, the same union spelling is not a union declaration and its multipart alternative is excluded there too.

A reference cycle closes through a schema position the artifact addresses but does not declare under components.schemas: `#/components/schemas/Wrapper/properties/inner` references itself. The cycle is a cycle wherever it closes, so the emitted operation schema must cut it at the addressed position and stay self-contained; emitting the artifact-space reference into the OBI would publish a reference that does not resolve in the emitted document (OBI-D-16). The operation is realizable and fully represented.

Whether a declared server URL denotes a target address at all decides whether the server configuration point is a runtime prerequisite of the represented target. A sole entry selects itself and, when it resolves, requires nothing. A sole entry whose URL template variable has no Server Variable Object never reduces to a URL -- the OAS substitutes only variables the Server Object declares, and braces appear in no RFC 3986 production -- while a declared variable's REQUIRED default always reduces. A sole entry whose http authority carries no host names no origin server, because RFC 9110 requires a recipient to reject such a URI as invalid. Each of those leaves the target address undetermined, and so does a multi-entry list with no selection, so all three raise configuration.server. Neither answer may be decided by a host language's URL parser: Go's net/url and the WHATWG parser disagree about exactly these two shapes, in opposite directions.

OAS 3.1.1 tabulates the Encoding Object default contentType for a part whose `type` is absent as application/octet-stream, in the first row of that field's own table. openbindings.openapi@1 defines no boundary from a JSON application value to octets for a form part, so a multipart alternative carrying such a part is an excluded alternative: uploadAvatar, whose only candidate is that alternative, is an excluded target; createNote keeps its JSON alternative and stays represented with the multipart alternative excluded; createLabel, whose part declares `type: string`, is unaffected. OAS 3.1.2 carries the same row verbatim and takes the same dispositions.

OAS 3.1.0 states the same answer as 3.1.1 for a part whose `type` is absent, by a different sentence: its Encoding Object contentType enumeration closes with a total catch-all — "for object - application/json; for array - the default is defined based on the inner type; for all other cases the default is application/octet-stream" — whose complement includes a declaration carrying no type at all. The dispositions are therefore the 3.1.1 ones, and this scenario exists because that ground is an implied answer rather than a tabulated row.

openbindings.openapi@1 section 6 composes the value AT the referenced JSON Pointer together with that value's transitive closure of references, and nothing else. A dangling reference in a component the pointer never reaches is outside that closure, so the referencing artifact resolves and its operation is represented. A whole-file composer refuses the same artifact.

openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

scenarios.description: The twin of the scenario above, differing only in which component carries the dangling reference. Reachable from the referenced pointer and unresolvable there, it makes the referencing artifact unresolvable, and the whole source refuses. The pair is what shows the pointer-scoped rule narrowed composition rather than merely widening acceptance.

scenarios.description: A sequence member is addressed by index exactly as an object member is addressed by name (RFC 6901 section 4). The composed value is allOf/0, so the defective allOf/1 beside it is outside the closure and the artifact resolves.

scenarios.description: Two references compose two elements of the same sequence and the defective element between them is composed by neither. Index identity has to survive that: allOf/2 must still denote the third element, so no index may be renumbered when one is left out. The two assertions are what distinguish surviving indices from a silently compacted sequence, which the operation set alone cannot see.

scenarios.description: Every accepted OAS 3.1 edition keys the application/octet-stream part default on a DECLARED string carrying `contentEncoding` — 3.1.0 as "a `type: string` with a `contentEncoding`", 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 as the Encoding Object default table's `string` row with contentEncoding present. On a declared non-string type the keyword is inert: the same table holds `n/a` in the contentEncoding column of the `number, integer, or boolean` and `object` rows, defined by its own note as "the presence or value of contentEncoding is irrelevant", and JSON Schema 2020-12 makes the Content vocabulary annotations that "do not function as validation assertions", each conditioned on a string instance. So recordSample and recordProfile keep the text/plain and application/json rows and are represented; uploadAvatar takes the encoded-string row and is represented; and only createNote's part, which declares no `type` at all, reaches the `type`-absent row's application/octet-stream, for which openbindings.openapi@1 defines no JSON-to-octet part boundary, so that alternative is excluded and its sole-candidate target with it. The excluded target carries `openapi.media_schema_mismatch` with no alternative entry beside it, which is the established accounting for a sole-candidate operation whose only alternative is excluded — the same shape OAPI-SS-23 pins for its `/avatars` target.

info.title: Content keywords on declared part types

scenarios.description: A reference's fragment addresses what looks like a sibling member of a $ref node, and on the 3.0 line there is no such member to address. The Reference Object is defined by JSON Reference, whose section 3 states that any members other than "$ref" in a JSON Reference object SHALL be ignored, so `Alias` has exactly one denotable member and the token `properties` cannot name the declared sibling. Evaluation therefore continues into the referenced value exactly as it does when no sibling is declared, and the emitted value is `Real`'s, not the sibling's. The assertion is the whole scenario: the operation set is identical under either reading, and only the value distinguishes them.

scenarios.description: The twin of the scenario above on a byte-identical artifact apart from the declared edition. No 3.1 edition incorporates JSON Reference; the 3.1 Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema 2020-12, whose section 8.2.3.1 carries the authors' note that other keywords can appear alongside "$ref" in the same schema object. The node keeps its own members, the token names one of them, and the composed value is the sibling. The pair is what shows the rule is the incorporated authority's and splits by edition line rather than being one averaged convention.

scenarios.description: The retention consequence of OAPI-SS-31's reading, as a defect, and the twin of OAPI-SS-34. On the 3.0 line the fragment's next token cannot name an ignored member, so what the pointer runs into is the reference itself: the reference is composed, its target is inside the closure, and a target that is never declared makes the whole source unresolvable. Nothing about the sibling's own shape changes that, which is what separates a reference the closure composes from one a pointer merely walks past.
